post.caption:
Life on station is decided by two facts: nothing falls, and nothing arrives cheaply. Water is recovered from sweat, breath condensation and urine at well over 90%. Bone remodels to match load, so with no load it thins continuously, which is why crews exercise around two hours a day just to slow it. Fluid stops pooling in the legs and shifts to the head, puffing faces and changing eyesight. All of it is the body responding exactly as the physics predicts.
